 2                THE SECRETARY:   Resolution Number 

 3   3237, by Senators LaValle and Seward, commending 

 4   the Civil Air Patrol-New York Wing Suffolk Cadet 

 5   Squadron 10 Color Guard upon the occasion of 

 6   presenting the colors at the start of the session 

 7   of the New York State Senate.  

 8                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

 9   Legislative Body to recognize that the quality 

10   and character of life in the communities across 

11   New York State are reflective of the concerned 

12   and dedicated efforts of those organizations and 

13   individuals who are devoted to the welfare of the 

14   community and its citizenry; and 

15                "WHEREAS, Attendant to such concern, 

16   and in full accord with its long-standing 

17   traditions, this Legislative Body is justly proud 

18   to commend the Suffolk Cadet Squadron 10 Color 

19   Guard from the Civil Air Patrol-New York Wing 

20   upon the occasion of presenting the colors at the 

21   start of the session of the New York State 

22   Senate, to be held at the New York State Capitol 

23   in Albany, New York; and 

24                "WHEREAS, The Civil Air Patrol 

25   enjoys a proud legacy of selfless sacrifice and 


                                                                65

 1   service to country and community that spans 

 2   decades; the organization was born one week prior 

 3   to the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor; and whose 

 4   members serving in World War Two were awarded the 

 5   Congressional Gold Medal; and 

 6                "WHEREAS, Thousands of volunteer 

 7   members of the Civil Air Patrol answered 

 8   America's call to national service and sacrifice 

 9   by accepting and performing critical wartime 

10   missions; and 

11                "WHEREAS, On July 1, 1946, President 

12   Harry S. Truman signed Public Law 476  

13   incorporating the Civil Air Patrol as a 

14   benevolent, nonprofit organization; on May 26, 

15   1948, Congress passed Public Law 557 permanently 

16   establishing the Civil Air Patrol as the 

17   auxiliary of the new United States Air Force; and 

18                "WHEREAS, Three primary mission 

19   areas were set forth at the inception of the 

20   Civil Air Patrol:  aerospace education, cadet 

21   programs, and emergency services; and 

22                "WHEREAS, Today, the Civil Air 

23   Patrol handles 90 percent of inland search and 

24   rescue missions, with approximately 75 lives 

25   saved each year; its members are generally the 


                                                                66

 1   first on the scene, transmitting aerial digital  

 2   images along with providing disaster relief and 

 3   emergency services following natural and manmade 

 4   disasters, including such events as 9/11, 

 5   Hurricane Katrina, Hurricane Irene, Tropical 

 6   Storm Lee, Texas and Oklahoma wildfires,  

 7   tornadoes in the south and central United States,  

 8   North Dakota flash flooding and the October 2006 

 9   earthquake in Hawaii, as well as humanitarian and 

10   homeland security missions along the United 

11   States and Mexico border; and 

12                "WHEREAS, In response to the 

13   devastating effects of Hurricane Sandy, the Civil 

14   Air Patrol's New York Wing promptly reacted by 

15   flying 373 damage assessment sorties and 

16   providing 143,360 aerial photographs to New York 

17   disaster relief organizations, FEMA, and the 

18   Army Corps of Engineers; providing air 

19   transportation throughout the affected region for  

20   disaster response teams; deploying 30 volunteers 

21   to assist with shelter operations conducted by 

22   the New York City Office of Emergency Management; 

23   and installing 40 volunteers to assist the 

24   Red Cross with the logistics of relief supplies; 

25   and 


                                                                67

 1                "WHEREAS, In addition, Civil Air  

 2   Patrol members are dedicated to counterdrug 

 3   reconnaissance and to teaching a new generation 

 4   about aerospace and its impact on our future; its 

 5   cadet programs ensure our youth receive the 

 6   finest leadership training the nation has to 

 7   offer; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, The members from the 

 9   Suffolk Cadet Squadron 10 Color Guard Civil Air 

10   Patrol-New York Wing include: Derek Profit, 

11   C/Capt.; Michael Russo, C/2nd Lt.; Alison 

12   Shumway, C/CMSgt.; Kevin Smith, C/CMSgt.; 

13   Kyle Velez, C/CMSgt.; Nick Molinelli, C/SMSgt.; 

14   Nicholas Volpe, C/MSgt.; Andrew Balistreri, 

15   Lt. Col.; Joseph Volpe, Capt.; Andreas Niens, 

16   1st Lt.; and New York Wing Staff Steven Perta, 

17   Colonel; Thomas Carello, Lt. Col.; Andrew Liddle, 

18   Lt. Col.; Patrick Magee, Lt. Col.; Gerald 

19   Marketos, Lt. Col.; and Benjamin Nodar, Lt. Col.; 

20   and 

21                "WHEREAS, The Civil Air Patrol makes 

22   a huge impact each and every day, going above and 

23   beyond to make a profound difference in America's 

24   communities; and 

25                "WHEREAS, This occasion presents a 


                                                                68

 1   unique opportunity for this Legislative Body to 

 2   recognize and pay tribute to the members of the 

 3   Civil Air Patrol-New York Wing Suffolk Cadet 

 4   Squadron 10 Color Guard; and 

 5                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

 6   Legislative Body that when organizations of such 

 7   noble aims and accomplishments are brought to our 

 8   attention, they should be recognized by all the 

 9   citizens of this great Empire State; now, 

10   therefore, be it 

11                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

12   Body pause in its deliberations to commend the 

13   Civil Air Patrol-New York Wing Suffolk Cadet 

14   Squadron 10 Color Guard and its members upon the 

15   occasion of presenting the colors at the start of 

16   the session of the New York State Senate; and be 

17   it further

19   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

20   Colonel Steven Perta, New York Wing commander, 

21   Civil Air Patrol, and the aforementioned members 

22   of the Suffolk Cadet Squadron 10 Color Guard 

23   Civil Air Patrol-New York Wing."

 7                SENATOR SEWARD:   Thank you,

 9                I'm very pleased to stand in support

15                And I'm very sorry that Lieutenant 

16   Colonel Andrew Liddle, who's a constituent of

18   tradition a few years ago, is not able to be with 

19   us today for health reasons.

20                But I'm very pleased to sponsor this 

21   resolution commending Lieutenant Colonel Andrew 

22   Liddle.

23                You know, we mainly think of the 

24   Civil Air Patrol as being of great assistance to 

25   New Yorkers, the New York Wing here in New York, 


                                                                72

 1   at a time when we need them most, whether it's a 

 2   search and rescue mission or a time of natural 

 3   disaster or even a manmade disaster.  The Civil 

 4   Air Patrol is always there working on behalf of 

 5   New Yorkers and helping to protect us, fulfilling 

 6   important roles in the most recent years from the 

 7   disasters of 9/11 to Hurricane Sandy.  Whatever 

 8   it is, the Civil Air Patrol is there to be of 

 9   assistance to New Yorkers.

10                But one of the additional services 

11   that they provide is sponsoring the cadet 

12   program, which is a wonderful program which is 

13   designed for young adults and is aimed at helping 

14   them to develop essential life skills and to 

15   instill such values as teamwork, personal 

16   integrity, leadership, respect, self-confidence, 

17   and the list goes on.  All great qualities that 

18   will assist these cadets throughout their entire 

19   life.

20                And this resolution before us, in 

21   honoring Lieutenant Colonel Andrew Liddle -- who 

22   as I said earlier was so instrumental in bringing 

23   the cadets to us a few years ago for the 

24   presentation of the colors -- he himself has had 

25   a distinguished career as a New Yorker.

 1                He graduated from the New York 

 2   Rangers School of the New York State College of 

 3   Forestry.  After graduation, he attended the 

 4   New York State Police Academy here in Albany, and 

 5   in 1966 he successfully completed the New York 

 6   State Instructor Development Program.

 7                He went on to serve his country as a 

 8   member of the United States Air Force.  And 

 9   during his time in the military he graduated from 

10   many Air Force colleges, completing various 

11   courses which would enable him to become a strong 

12   leader in our state.  And throughout the years, 

13   Andy Liddle held numerous positions in various 

14   fields, utilizing his vast education and 

15   experience.

17   affiliated with the Civil Air Patrol, holding the 

18   title of United States Air Force Auxiliary 

19   Lieutenant Colonel.  And throughout his tenure he 

20   acted as the government relations advisor to both 

21   the New York Wing and the entire Northeast 

22   Region.

23                And I'm very sorry he's not able to 

24   be with us today for health reasons.  But we, 

25   through this resolution that we are adopting

10                SENATOR KRUEGER:   Thank you, 

11   Mr. President.

12                So this is the same bill we've seen 

13   and I believe passed in this house I don't even 

14   know how many times now, since we tend to pass 

15   bills over and over again as one-house bills.  

16                I continue to object to this bill.  

17   It would be establishing a radically higher tax 

18   deduction for a certain form of philanthropic 

19   giving, leaving the State of New York with a 

20   situation where philanthropic giving for most 

21   nonprofit purposes would have X percentage for 

22   tax deductibility and for this purpose having 

23   something like 10, 20, 30 times that tax 

24   deductibility.  So as a precedent, it's a 

25   dangerous one of uneven treatment under the law 


                                                                83

 1   for charitable giving.

 2                Second, it actually moves taxpayers' 

 3   dollars away from the state to determine where 

 4   they ought to go and into selected private 

 5   educational facilities, directed by the donor.  I 

 6   don't think that's how we ought to fund education 

 7   in the State of New York with taxpayers' dollars.

 8                It challenges a series of 

 9   potentially constitutional questions about uses 

10   of public monies for religious purposes which 

11   have never been fully addressed in all the 

12   different debates that we have had in this house.  

13                I suspect this won't be the last 

14   time I see this bill this year.  I hope before 

15   the next time I see it we try something called 

16   the committee process, where it goes through 

17   appropriate committees.  I would think this bill 

18   ought to go through, at minimum, the 

19   Investigations Committee, because it's a tax 

20   bill; the Education Committee, because it 

21   directly impacts education; and the Finance 

22   Committee, because it's taking of state taxpayer 

23   money.

24                So maybe we will have committees 

25   evaluate this bill.  Maybe this is even the kind
